one_liner: Surge's 8-tap table-driven SSE Lanczos stereo resampler for real-time audio; claimed about 2x faster than libsamplerate's fastest sinc.
what_it_does: sst::basic_blocks::dsp::LanczosResampler<blockSize> is a header-only streaming sample-rate converter for stereo float audio, built for 'resample 48k to variable rate with a small window' inside the Surge synth libraries. You construct it with input and output rates, push(L, R) one frame at a time into a 4096-frame ring buffer, then pull with populateNext(outL, outR, max) or the unchecked block variants (populateNextBlockSize, the 2x oversampled populateNextBlockSizeOS, and linear or zero-order-hold versions). The API is unrelated to libsamplerate's src_process and SRC_DATA, so it is not a drop-in.
how_it_is_fast: It is Lanczos interpolation with A = 4, so each output frame is an 8-tap dot product. The windowed-sinc kernel is precomputed into a static table of 8,193 fractional phases by 8 taps, plus a table of deltas for linear interpolation between phases, so no sin() is evaluated at run time. Each read loads two 4-wide coefficient vectors, blends them with the deltas, multiplies them against two unaligned SSE loads per channel and finishes with a horizontal sum. The stereo pair shares one coefficient computation, and the ring buffer is stored twice so reads never wrap. libsamplerate's SRC_SINC_FASTEST instead convolves about 39 taps per output (half length 2,463 at increment 128, derived from src_sinc.c and fastest_coeffs.h) and widens the filter by 1/ratio when downsampling, so much of the speed gap comes from doing less filtering.
when_to_use: Real-time stereo audio in a plugin or synth (JUCE, iPlug-style code) that needs variable or non-integer rate conversion, for example host rate to a fixed 48 kHz engine rate, with only a few samples of latency (it needs A + 1 = 5 input frames ahead of the read point).
Upsampling, or ratios close to 1 (44.1k and 48k), where an 8-tap kernel is acceptable and anti-aliasing matters little.
Code already inside the Surge, Shortcircuit or sst-* stack, where setup.h and SIMDe are already present.
Non-GPL projects that need a small permissive resampler: this header is dual-licensed MIT/GPL-3.0, unlike the rest of the repo.
when_not_to_use: Downsampling material with content above the output Nyquist (96k to 48k, 48k to 44.1k): the kernel is not widened with the ratio, so there is no anti-aliasing low-pass and energy between the two Nyquist frequencies aliases. libsoxr, r8brain-free-src or libsamplerate's sinc modes filter it.
Mastering or offline conversion where measured SNR or passband specs matter: no quality figures are published, and the unit tests only bound the error on a slow sine (|d| < 0.025).
Mono, multichannel (more than 2), double-precision or integer audio: the class is hard-wired to two float channels.
Callers that push more than about 4,000 frames before reading: the 4096-frame ring buffer overwrites unread input without any check.
Choosing on the 2x speed claim alone: no reproducible benchmark of this header exists (see verified_claims_summary).

integration.dependencies: sst/basic-blocks/simd/setup.h and mechanics/simd-ops.h (GPL-3.0-or-later); SIMDe on non-x86 targets (without the simde CMake target the build is x86-64 only). For MIT use, copy the header, drop both includes, map SIMD_MM(x) to _mm_x and replace sum_ps_to_float with a horizontal add.
integration.min_toolchain: C++20 (setup.h static_asserts __cplusplus >= 202002L); on MSVC, needs _USE_MATH_DEFINES for M_PI (the CMake target sets it on WIN32). A stripped MIT copy's minimum standard is not documented.
integration.platforms: x86-64 (SSE2 native); arm64 and Windows arm64ec through SIMDe
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. From the code, an instance has mutable state and is single-threaded; the shared static coefficient tables are filled lazily in the constructor behind a plain bool, so constructing the first instance of a given blockSize on two threads at once is a data race.

gotchas: The tables are static per template instantiation: each distinct blockSize carries two 8,193 x 8 float tables (about 512 KiB, derived from the declarations), and each instance holds a 64 KiB stereo ring buffer. The header's own 'Fixme: Make this static and shared' notes this.

populateNextBlockSize, populateNextBlockSizeOS and the Lin/ZOH variants do no range checks ('dangerous but efficient'); call inputsRequiredToGenerateOutputs first, and note that its source comment still reads 'Check this calculation'.

Bug history: #63 (2023-09) fixed a wrapped derivative table that caused occasional clicks on 44.1/48 round trips (found at iPlug); #83 (2024-01) fixed a memset that left the right channel's buffer uninitialised; #148 (2024-12) fixed an index error in a then-unused function. Copies of the code taken before late 2023, such as the 2021 copy vendored in NonIntegerSRC, may still carry the first bug.
The read is centred one sample behind the newest pushed frame, so there is a fixed latency of a few samples; phases are doubles that callers must renormalize (renormalizePhases) on long runs.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over libsoxr, r8brain-free-src or LibFResample when you need a tiny MIT-licensable, push/pull, low-latency stereo interpolator inside a real-time synth and can accept 8-tap quality. Pick those siblings, or NonIntegerSRC's Holters-Parker resampler (17-40x over SRC_SINC_FASTEST in its own chart), when you need band-limited downsampling or published speed and quality numbers.
verified_claims_summary: The only figure is an unanswered user question (NonIntegerSRC issue 4, 2026-05-18) saying Lanczos ran about 2x faster than 'Sinc' (the harness's libsamplerate SRC_SINC_FASTEST, mono) on an unnamed machine, with no timings, compiler or flags. The harness times a 2021 mono Surge copy (src/src_utils/LanczosResampler.h), not this header, and that copy is buggy: its table has 8,192 rows but is indexed up to 8,192, so every exactly integer read position reads past the array. That is every output for 96k to 48k (dPhaseO = 2.0) and every other output for 48k to 96k (dPhaseO = 0.5). The harness computes but never prints error statistics, so the wrong output went unnoticed (the current sst-basic-blocks header sizes the table at tableObs + 1 and is correct).
status_note: Actively maintained as the bottom layer of the Surge libraries (last commit 2026-09-27, 10 commits to this header, counting the April 2023 move from Surge); the header is copyable under MIT once the GPL simd includes are replaced, but it has no benchmark of its own.
